clue.text: Power and sway diminish little by little

indicators.note: to sway is to swing or waver, so the two words before it are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: A ruler's authority and influence gradually wane over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sway' looks like a noun paired with power, but it is the anagram signal working on POWER AND.
explanation.definitionFit: To trim something away gradually, reducing it bit by bit, is a phrasal verb synonym of cutting back slowly.

clue.text: Switch sides after turning up for military action

indicators.note: after places the switch letters following the turned word
turning means the little word up is read backwards
sides are the first and last letters of switch

explanation.surface: A soldier changes allegiance after an advance turns things around.
explanation.definitionFit: A push is an advance or offensive by an army, a military noun.

clue.text: Attachment to identify bird call

definitions.meaning: a band fitted on a bird's leg for tracking

explanation.surface: A tag for identifying a bird's song.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds are tagged with a leg band, and to phone someone is to give them a buzz.

clue.text: Sir Henry's revolutionary work in popular music of the 1950s

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the conductor's surname is read backwards

parts.note: Sir Henry Wood was the British conductor who founded the Proms
op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A conductor's radical composition belongs to a 1950s pop style.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Henry Wood founded London's Proms concerts.
explanation.definitionFit: This vocal-harmony style is a genre of 1950s popular music.

clue.text: One intent on layout not outlay?

definitions.text: One intent on layout not outlay?

parts.words: One intent on layout not outlay?
parts.note: someone who looks at shop displays but does not spend money

explanation.definitionFit: Such a person admires arrangements of goods in shops without buying, browsing rather than spending.

clue.text: Snoops around for sign of Zorro's treasures

indicators.note: the prying word is wrapped around the masked hero's mark

parts.note: to snoop is to pry, so snoops means pries
Zorro famously slashes a Z as his sign

explanation.surface: A nosy person searches for Zorro's mark to find his hidden hoard.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasures are things highly valued, synonym of the plural noun for cherished rewards.

clue.text: Damn! Outlaw's given sweetheart poison

parts.note: rats is an exclamation of annoyance like damn
to outlaw is to ban
the heart of sweet is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Cursing, a bandit gives his lover poison.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old name for rat poison, often arsenic.

clue.text: Begin a Zola novel? That's sweet

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Starting one of Zola's books is a pleasant experience.
explanation.walkthrough: Zola's novels tempt a reading of 'novel' as a book; it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian whipped dessert of egg, sugar and wine is an example of a sweet.

clue.text: Tintin's dog regrets taking wings off bird

parts.note: Snowy is the white dog in the Tintin comics

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its outer letters, here removed from regrets

explanation.surface: Tintin's dog is sorry for plucking the wings off a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This white American heron is an example of a bird.

clue.text: Poem about a Parisian bishop giving capital protection

indicators.note: the poem goes about, or around, the French article and the bishop

parts.note: a sonnet is a fourteen-line poem
a Parisian would say un for a
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: Verses about a French cleric are offered as protection for a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' here means head, not a city: the hat protects the head from sun.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital is an old word for the head, and this brimmed hat shields the head from sunshine.

clue.text: Everyone has to make up a radio programme

parts.note: the world can mean everybody
to atone is to make up for a wrong

explanation.surface: Everybody must reconcile, says a radio show.
explanation.walkthrough: The World at One is a BBC Radio 4 lunchtime news programme.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a long-running BBC lunchtime news broadcast, an example of radio programming.

clue.text: Forbidden expressions of gratitude and disapproval

parts.note: ta is an informal British way of saying thanks
boo is a jeer of disapproval

explanation.surface: Some words of thanks and of jeering are banned.
explanation.definitionFit: Something forbidden by custom or prohibition is off-limits, an adjective synonym.

clue.text: March: the Spanish score

parts.note: the punctuation mark printed in the clue is itself a colon
el is Spanish for the
a bogey is a golf score of one over par

explanation.surface: A musical march is followed by mention of a Spanish tally.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon after March is not punctuation but a piece of wordplay. COLONEL BOGEY is a famous British military march.
explanation.definitionFit: This well-known tune is an example of a military marching piece, famous from a war film.

clue.text: Video game for male hairdresser?

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
a braider plaits hair

explanation.surface: Is there a video game featuring a male hair stylist?
explanation.definitionFit: This adventure series starring Lara Croft is a well-known computer game.

clue.text: In a test venue, a punishment for pupils displaying arrogance

indicators.note: in places the punishment inside the cricket ground

parts.note: Lord's in London hosts Test cricket matches
lines are sentences a pupil must copy out as punishment

explanation.surface: At a cricket ground, a schoolboy's penalty shows his haughtiness.
explanation.walkthrough: LORD'S is a London cricket ground where Test matches are played; 'lines' are a British school punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Haughty arrogance is lordly behaviour, so the abstract noun is a synonym.

clue.text: Music producer in love with broker, oddly

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like the letter O

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third and fifth letters of the word broker

explanation.surface: A record producer is in love with a stockbroker, strangely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Music producer' suggests a person in the record industry; it is an instrument that produces music.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodwind instrument produces music, so it is cryptically called a music producer.

clue.text: A nautical measure? Time aboard is incredible

indicators.note: aboard means on board, inside, so the time letter goes inside the measure

parts.note: a sounding is a measurement of water depth taken from a ship

explanation.surface: A sailor's depth measurement taken while time is aboard ship turns out amazing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something astonishing is hard to believe, an adjective synonym of amazing.

clue.text: Screaming habdabs breaking out this year?

indicators.note: breaking out suggests the letters burst apart and reform

explanation.surface: Panic is erupting this year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screaming habdabs' is British slang for a state of extreme nervous panic.
explanation.definitionFit: The screaming habdabs is British slang for frantic panic, a synonym of uncontrolled emotional excess.

clue.text: Friend and companion of Ivy, a lamented singer

parts.note: a buddy is a friend
holly and ivy are paired, as in the Christmas carol

explanation.surface: A friend and Ivy's partner are mourned as a singer.
explanation.walkthrough: Buddy Holly was an American rock and roll singer who died in a 1959 plane crash, hence 'lamented'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rock and roll star died young in an air crash, so he is a mourned vocalist.

clue.text: Head expelling blockhead formerly

indicators.note: expelling means throwing out, so a letter is removed from the head word

parts.note: bonce is British slang for the head
read as block's head, its first letter B

explanation.surface: A school head expels a dim pupil, as happened in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: BONCE is British slang for head; 'blockhead' is read as the head, or first letter, of 'block'.
explanation.definitionFit: Formerly means at one time in the past, an adverb synonym.

clue.text: Work at last for engineers on list

indicators.note: on places the engineers on top of the list in this down clue

parts.note: RE stands for Royal Engineers
a ship that lists heels over to one side

explanation.surface: Instructions for engineers on a schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: A last is a cobbler's foot-shaped block, so working at it means fitting new heels on shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cobbler fixes new heels to shoes on a last, so this is work done at one.

clue.text: Dramatist or thespian — as in play

indicators.note: in play suggests the letters are moved around, as in a drama or game

explanation.surface: A playwright or an actor appears in a stage production.
explanation.walkthrough: Aristophanes was an ancient Greek comic dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Athenian comic playwright is an example of a dramatist.

clue.text: Currency in "The Grapes of Wrath"

indicators.note: in indicates the letters are found within the title words

explanation.surface: Money mentioned in Steinbeck's novel about the Dust Bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the monetary unit of Mexico and several other countries.

clue.text: German king unaffected by revolution

indicators.note: the name reads the same when turned backwards

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A German monarch survived an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: Otto I was a medieval German king and Holy Roman Emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto the Great was a tenth-century ruler of the Germans.

clue.text: Gloomy dean's head and backside

indicators.note: the head of the word dean is its first letter

parts.note: rear is a word for backside

explanation.surface: A college dean's head and bottom are both dismal.
explanation.definitionFit: Drear is a poetic adjective synonym of dreary, meaning dismal.

clue.text: One president or another? That's tricky to resolve

indicators.note: tricky suggests the letters are awkward and need sorting out

explanation.surface: Naming one American president or another is a hard puzzle to solve.
explanation.walkthrough: There were two US presidents named Roosevelt, Theodore and Franklin, hence 'one or another'.
explanation.definitionFit: Two American leaders, Theodore and Franklin, shared this surname, so it names either of them.

clue.text: Caribbean capital, pink and gold

parts.note: rose is a shade of pink
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A Caribbean city is described in pink and gold colours.
explanation.walkthrough: Roseau is the capital of Dominica.
explanation.definitionFit: This town is the capital city of Dominica, an island in the Caribbean.

clue.text: Prosperous — or upset by depression?

indicators.note: by means next to, so the fuss sits beside the hollow

parts.note: a well is a hole or depression in the ground
a to-do is a fuss or upset

explanation.surface: Is a rich person really troubled by low spirits?
explanation.definitionFit: Being comfortably off means wealthy, an adjective synonym.
